title: The Mona Lisa Was Stolen?! A New Musical Is Coming!
summary: Have you ever stared at the Mona Lisa and thought, "What if someone just… took it?" Well, in 1911, that actually happened! And now, Andrew Lloyd Webber—the guy behind huge musicals like The Phantom of the Opera—is writing a show about it. He's the king of big, wild musicals. Think underground lakes, singing cats, and Egyptian pharaohs. Now he's tackling the world's most famous painting. The Mona Lisa is tiny, only 30 inches tall, but millions visit her at the Louvre in Paris. Back in 1911, she was already getting love letters from fans! The museum put her behind glass for safety. But one of the workers installing the glass, an Italian named Vincenzo Peruggia, knew exactly how to remove her. On August 21, 1911, he slipped on a worker's smock, took the painting, and hid it in a stairwell. Nobody noticed for 28 hours! People freaked out. Thousands lined up just to stare at the empty wall. Even the famous writer Franz Kafka came. The police even questioned Pablo Picasso! For two years, the Mona Lisa was missing. Peruggia had stashed her in a trunk in his apartment. Finally, he tried to sell her back to Italy, claiming he wanted to return her to her home country. He was caught, and the painting became a superstar. Lloyd Webber says the musical is a true story about how the Mona Lisa disappeared and ended up in Italy. He's already super busy with other shows, but he's sneaking away to write this one. I can't wait to see how he turns this art heist into a musical spectacle!
why_it_matters: This story shows that even famous artworks have wild adventures, and history can be turned into an exciting show you might one day see on stage.

background_read: The Mona Lisa is a portrait painted by Leonardo da Vinci over 500 years ago and is one of the most famous paintings in the world.
Andrew Lloyd Webber (the composer of hit musicals like Cats and The Phantom of the Opera) is known for turning dramatic stories into big stage shows.
When the Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre (Paris's enormous art museum), the empty wall became a sensation—thousands came to see the spot, including the writer Franz Kafka.
Article_Structure: WHO: Andrew Lloyd Webber, a famous musical composer, and Vincenzo Peruggia, the thief.
WHAT: Webber is creating a musical about the real 1911 theft of the Mona Lisa.
WHERE: The theft happened at the Louvre museum in Paris, France.
WHY: Because the true story of the hidden painting, a worker in a smock, and the chase across two countries is full of drama.

perspectives.description: A new show from Andrew Lloyd Webber is thrilling because his musicals always have amazing songs and surprising stage effects—the theft story will be full of suspense.
Some might worry that a comedy musical about a theft might not respect the painting's importance, but it could also get more people interested in art history.
The theft actually made the Mona Lisa super famous—before 1911, it was not the most well-known painting. A strange crime changed how the world sees it forever.
